title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
summary: There is a fixed $\theta < 1$ with no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s > \theta$. An OpenAI manuscript dated 30 September 2026 claims every Dirichlet $L$-function, $\zeta$ included, is zero-free in $\operatorname{Re}s > \tfrac78$, using Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and cubic theta sums. The 7/8 version was reported as Lean-verified; a second proof gives $\tfrac{11}{12}$. Community verification is ongoing.
why: A width that does not shrink with height changes the error term in the prime number theorem from $e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}}$-type savings to a power saving.

title: Exclusion of Siegel zeros
summary: A short paper in the 6 October 2026 release separately claims there are no exceptional zeros near $1$. The quasi-RH claim gives the same conclusion, so two independent routes were offered. Independent checking is under way.
why: If confirmed, ineffective constants in many theorems, Siegel–Walfisz included, become effective.

title: The twin prime conjecture
summary: There are infinitely many primes $p$ with $p + 2$ prime. Hardy and Littlewood conjectured the count up to $x$ is about $2C_2\,x/(\log x)^2$ with $C_2 \approx 0.6602$. Bounded gaps (246) is the best unconditional result.
why: Sieve theory's parity problem is the known barrier.

title: Goldbach's conjecture
summary: Every even integer greater than $2$ is a sum of two primes (Goldbach to Euler, 1742). Verified by computer far beyond $10^{18}$; the ternary version was proved by Helfgott in 2013.
why: The circle method handles three primes; two primes falls on the wrong side of the minor-arc barrier.

title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
summary: The rank of the group of rational points of an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb Q$ equals the order of vanishing of $L(E,s)$ at $s=1$. Known when that order is $0$ or $1$ (Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin).
why: It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems and would give an algorithm for deciding whether a cubic curve has infinitely many rational points.
references: Silverman & Tate, Rational Points on Elliptic Curves
Carlson, Jaffe & Wiles (eds.), The Millennium Prize Problems

title: P versus NP
summary: Is every problem whose solutions can be checked in polynomial time also solvable in polynomial time? Most researchers expect $\mathrm P \ne \mathrm{NP}$; known proof techniques (relativisation, natural proofs, algebrisation) provably cannot settle it.
why: A Millennium Prize Problem; modern cryptography assumes the answer is no.
references: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation
Carlson, Jaffe & Wiles (eds.), The Millennium Prize Problems

title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
summary: Do smooth initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations always give a smooth solution for all time? Leray (1934) constructed weak solutions; their uniqueness and regularity are open.
why: A Millennium Prize Problem about the basic equations of fluid flow.
references: Carlson, Jaffe & Wiles (eds.), The Millennium Prize Problems

title: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
summary: Construct a quantum Yang–Mills theory on $\mathbb R^4$ for any compact simple gauge group satisfying the standard axioms, and prove it has a mass gap $\Delta > 0$.
why: A Millennium Prize Problem; it asks for a mathematical foundation for the theory that describes the strong force.

title: The Hodge conjecture
summary: On a non-singular complex projective variety, every rational cohomology class of type $(p,p)$ is a rational combination of classes of algebraic subvarieties.
key_statements: H^{2p}(X,\mathbb Q)\cap H^{p,p}(X) \overset{?}{=} \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{[Z] : Z \subset X \text{ algebraic}\}
why: A Millennium Prize Problem connecting topology, analysis and algebra on the same space.
references: Carlson, Jaffe & Wiles (eds.), The Millennium Prize Problems

title: The Poincaré conjecture
summary: Every simply connected closed $3$-manifold is homeomorphic to the $3$-sphere. Proved by Perelman (2002–03) using Ricci flow with surgery; the only Millennium Problem solved.
why: Perelman declined both the Fields Medal (2006) and the Millennium Prize (2010).
references: Carlson, Jaffe & Wiles (eds.), The Millennium Prize Problems
